doc.title: Tom Porrello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 6, 2023

title: Joining the musicians' union in Easton at 16
summary: Plays in his father's dance band; joins the Easton union for about five dollars with no audition.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Yeah. My father also had like the number one of then back in those days they called it the dance bands. So he was like the most popular band in town. So I started playing with that also, that when I was 16 because I had to join the union and I had to wait ‘til I was 16.
I was going to ask about that, do you remember what it cost? This would have been a union of which city?
Okay. What did it cost to join the union, can you recall? Say that again?
And did you have to audition?
Yeah. Just like “What do you play?” “Trumpet” “How many valves?” “Three.” “You’re in.”
You got it. Like they say it must be an easy instrument to play because you’ve only got three things to push. © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
